stages.name: Red
stages.big: Counting, seeing small numbers, more and fewer, parts of 5, one more and one less, zero

stages.name: Orange
stages.big: Five and a bit, bonds to 10, doubles, odd and even, numerals, shape, pattern and measures

stages.name: Yellow
stages.big: Ten and a bit, place value, arrays, square and step numbers, bridging 10, sharing and grouping

stages.name: Green
stages.big: Rectangles and factors, counting in 10s and 5s, the 3, 4 and 5 times tables

stages.name: Blue
stages.big: Numbers to 100 and beyond, tens and ones, 6 to 9 times tables, fractions

units.title: Meet One to Three
units.idea: Each number is a group of that many blocks.
checks: Gives you 1, 2 or 3 objects when asked
Says which of two small groups has more
prompts: How many blocks is Two made of? Show me with your fingers.
Three came along. Is Three more or less than Two?
What happens when One joins Two?

activity.materials: Building blocks or cubes; a small bowl
steps: Build One, Two and Three as towers.
Ask her to hand you "two blocks", then "three".
Put 2 and 3 side by side: which tower has more?

units.title: Four and Five
units.idea: Counting tells us how many; the last number we say is the answer.
checks: Counts 5 objects and answers "how many?" with the last number
Orders towers 1 to 5 and finds a missing one
prompts: Four is a square. Can you make a square with 4 blocks?
Five has a hand. How many fingers are on one hand?
Which number is missing: 1, 2, _, 4, 5?

steps: Build towers 1 to 5 and line them up like a staircase.
Hide one tower; she finds which is missing.
Count 5 toys together, then ask "so how many?"

units.title: How counting works
units.idea: One number word for each thing, in the same order every time; moving things does not change how many.
checks: Says a rearranged group is still the same number
Recognises 1 to 4 dots without counting
prompts: Does Three change if she stands in a line or a triangle?
How did you know it was four so quickly?

activity.materials: Five buttons; dot cards or a dice
steps: Count 5 buttons in a line, then spread them out: "How many now?"
Flash dice faces 1 to 4 for a second each; she says the number.
Let her be the teacher and catch you miscounting.

units.title: Inside 1 to 5
units.idea: Numbers are made of smaller numbers: 5 can be 4 and 1, or 3 and 2.
checks: Splits 5 blocks two different ways and names the parts
prompts: Five split into two parts. What were the parts?
Can you make Four out of two Twos?
Is there another way to split Five?

steps: Snap the tower of 5 into two pieces.
Say the parts together: "3 and 2 make 5".
Find as many ways as you can and lay them out in a pattern.

units.title: One more, one less, none
units.idea: Adding one makes the next number; taking one away makes the one before; nothing at all is zero.
checks: Says one more and one less for numbers up to 5
Uses "zero" for an empty set and "more"/"fewer" correctly
prompts: Three fell in a hole and lost a block. Who did she become?
If there are no blocks left, what number is that?
Who is bigger, Two or Four? How do you know?

activity.materials: Blocks; a cup to hide blocks under
steps: Show 3 blocks, hide one under the cup: "How many now?"
Add one back: "One more than 2 is…?"
Take all away: "How many blocks are left?" (zero)

units.title: Sort and classify
units.idea: Things can be grouped by colour, shape, size — and we can say our rule.
checks: Sorts objects by one property and says the rule
Sorts by two properties (e.g. colour, then size)
prompts: What rule did you use?
Can you sort the same things a different way?

activity.materials: Mixed buttons, blocks or kitchen items
steps: Sort by colour and name the groups.
Mix them up; sort again by size.
You sort secretly; she guesses your rule.

units.title: Stage 1 review
units.idea: A mixed look back at numbers 0 to 5.
checks: Counts, compares and splits numbers to 5 in a mixed game
prompts: Which Numberblock is your favourite and what can it do?
Show me Four in two different ways.

steps: Roll the dice: she builds that Numberblock.
Ask one question each time: one more? one less? split it?
Swap roles: she asks you.

units.title: Meet Six to Ten
units.idea: Numbers keep growing one block at a time, up to Ten.
checks: Counts 10 objects reliably
Recognises dice and ten-frame patterns to 10
prompts: Six likes dice. Show me six on a dice.
Ten is made of how many Ones?
Nine looks like a square. How many on each side?

steps: Fill the ten-frame one counter at a time, counting aloud.
Make 7 on the frame; ask how many empty spaces.
Build Six to Ten as towers and line them up.

units.title: Counting on and back
units.idea: Counting forwards adds one each time; counting back takes one away.
checks: Counts back from 10 to 0
Says one more and one less within 10
Counts in 2s to 10
prompts: Blast off! Count down from 10 with me.
If we start at 6 and add one, where do we land?
Two goes up the tree in jumps of 2. Where does she land?

activity.materials: A number track 0–10 (chalk on the floor or paper)
steps: She jumps along the track counting on from any number.
Count back to 0 for a rocket launch.

units.title: Comparing to 10
units.idea: We can say which number is greater and find how many more.
checks: Says which of two numbers to 10 is greater or less
Finds the difference between two towers
prompts: Which tower is taller? By how many blocks?
Is 8 greater than or less than 6?

steps: Build two towers; she says which is greater.
Line them up and count the extra blocks: that is the difference.
Find both numbers on the number line.

units.title: Five and a bit; bonds to 10
units.idea: Six to nine are five and a bit; pairs of numbers make ten.
checks: Sees 7 as 5 and 2 without counting
Says the partner to make 10 for any number
prompts: Seven is Five and…?
Ten split in two. What were the parts?
If 6 are hiding, how many are showing out of 10?

activity.materials: Ten-frame and two colours of counters; or 10 fingers
steps: Show 7 on fingers: one full hand and 2.
Fill the ten-frame with two colours and say the pair (6 and 4).
Hide some of 10 under a cloth; she says how many are hidden.

units.title: Equal groups, doubles, odd and even
units.idea: Numbers can be split into equal groups; even numbers make pairs, odd numbers have one left over.
checks: Says doubles up to 5 + 5
Sorts numbers to 10 into odd and even by pairing blocks
prompts: Double Two is…?
Can Seven make pairs? Who is left over?
Nine made three groups of three. Show me.

steps: Pair up socks or blocks: any left over? Then it is odd.
Build a double with two equal towers and count them.
Share 6 blocks between 2 teddies, then 3 teddies.

units.title: Numerals and quick recognition
units.idea: Each number has a written shape we can read and write.
checks: Reads and writes 0 to 9
Names small quantities on sight
prompts: Which numeral is that?
Can you write Five in the air, then on paper?

activity.materials: Paper, crayon; sand or salt tray
steps: Trace numerals 0–9 in sand.
Match numeral cards to groups of objects.
Write the number of something in the room (chairs, windows).

units.title: Shape, space and pattern
units.idea: Shapes have sides and corners; patterns repeat.
checks: Names common 2D and 3D shapes
Uses position words (on, under, behind, between)
Continues a repeating pattern
prompts: How many corners does a triangle have?
What shape is a ball? A box?
What comes next in red, blue, red, blue…?

activity.materials: Paper shapes; boxes, balls and tins from the kitchen
steps: Shape hunt: find 3 circles and 3 rectangles at home.
Hide a toy and give position clues.
Make a bead or block pattern; she continues it.

units.title: Measures and money
units.idea: We can compare how long or heavy things are, and use coins to pay.
checks: Compares two lengths or weights directly
Pays a small amount with coins
prompts: Which is taller, you or the door handle?
Which is heavier — how could we find out?

activity.materials: String; two bags; a few coins
steps: Compare two objects by standing them side by side.
Hold one bag in each hand: which is heavier?
Play a tiny shop with toys priced 1 to 5.

units.title: Money in rupees
units.idea: Indian coins and notes, and making amounts.
checks: Identifies ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20
Makes an amount up to ₹20 in two ways
Adds notes and coins up to ₹100
prompts: Which coin is worth more?
How else could you pay ₹10?

activity.materials: Real coins and notes up to ₹100
steps: Sort coins by value.
Price toys ₹1–₹20 and play shop.
Later: pay ₹45 with notes and coins, and count the change.

units.title: Measure with hands, cups and rods
units.idea: We can measure with our hands, feet and cups, then with one fixed unit.
checks: Estimates and checks a length with hand spans or footsteps
Measures with one uniform unit (a rod or pencil)
prompts: How many hand spans long is the table? Guess first!
Why did a grown-up get a different answer with their bigger hand?

activity.materials: Hands, feet, a cup, a pencil
steps: Guess, then measure the bed in footsteps.
Fill a bottle with cups of water and count.
Measure the same table with a pencil; compare with hand spans.

units.title: Reasoning with numbers to 10
units.idea: We can explain why an answer is right.
checks: Explains an answer using blocks ("it is 6 because…")
prompts: How do you know?
Could there be another answer?

steps: Set a riddle: "I am one more than 5 and one less than 7."
She builds the answer and explains.
She makes up a riddle for you.

units.title: Numbers in our languages
units.idea: Number names in our home languages, and number rhymes of our own.
checks: Counts to 10 in a home language
Makes up a short number rhyme or story
prompts: How do your grandparents count to ten?
Can you make a rhyme about Three?

steps: Count steps in your home language and in English.
Read numerals aloud in both languages.
Make up a 4-line counting rhyme together.

units.title: Equal rows: arrays to 12
units.idea: Some numbers make neat rectangles of equal rows.
checks: Builds 6, 8 and 12 as rectangles
Finds a number that cannot make a rectangle
prompts: How many rows? How many in each row?
Can Seven make a rectangle?

steps: Make 12 into rectangles: 2 rows of 6, 3 of 4…
Try 7: what happens?
Spot arrays at home: egg trays, windows.

units.title: Ten and a bit: 11 to 15
units.idea: Eleven to fifteen are ten and some more.
checks: Builds 13 as 10 and 3
Builds step numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15
prompts: Thirteen is Ten and…?
Fifteen is a step squad. Can you build the steps?

steps: Build 11–15 with one ten-stick and ones.
Say each as "ten and three".
Build staircases 1, 1+2, 1+2+3…

units.title: Place value to 15
units.idea: In 14, the 1 means one ten and the 4 means four ones.
checks: Reads 14 as one ten and four ones
Adds within 15 using the ten
prompts: What does the 1 in 14 stand for?
Ten and how many make 12?

steps: Show 14 with cubes and with cards (10 and 4 overlapped).
Make 12, 15, 11 the same way.
Ten plus a number: quick-fire game.

units.title: Sixteen to Twenty
units.idea: Up to twenty — two tens.
checks: Counts forwards and back from any number to 20
Says 20 is two tens
Builds square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16
prompts: Twenty is two…?
Count back from 17 to 9.
Sixteen is a square. How many on each side?

steps: Fill two ten-frames to make 20.
Start counting from 13, then back from 18.
Build the squares 1, 4, 9, 16.

units.title: Time and calendar
units.idea: Days, months, and o'clock on a clock.
checks: Names the days of the week in order
Reads o'clock and half past
Finds today's date on a calendar
prompts: What day comes after Friday?
What time is it when the long hand points to 12?

activity.materials: A wall calendar; a clock with hands
steps: Cross off each day on the calendar.
Set the clock to meal times.
Talk about yesterday, today, tomorrow.

units.title: Multiplication and division
units.idea: Multiplying is adding equal groups; dividing is sharing or grouping.
checks: Shows 3 groups of 4
Shares 12 equally between 3
Groups 12 into 3s
prompts: How many groups? How many in each?
Share 12 sweets with 4 friends. How many each?

steps: Make 3 plates of 4: how many in all?
Share 12 onto 4 plates.
Make groups of 3 from 12: how many groups?

units.title: Bonds to 20; bridging 10
units.idea: Make ten first to add past ten.
checks: Solves 8 + 5 by making 10 first
prompts: 8 needs how many to make 10?
8 + 5: make 10, then how many more?

steps: Show 8 + 5 on two ten-frames.
Move 2 across to fill the first frame.
Say: "10 and 3 is 13."

units.title: Odd, even; 1 and 2 times tables
units.idea: Counting in 2s gives the even numbers.
checks: Counts in 2s to 20
Sorts numbers to 20 as odd or even
prompts: Is 15 odd or even? How do you know?
Count shoes in pairs: 2, 4, 6…

steps: Count shoes in 2s.
Hop along even numbers on a floor track.
Sort numeral cards 1–20 into odd and even.

units.title: Into the twenties: rectangles and factors
units.idea: Bigger numbers can make many rectangles.
checks: Finds all the rectangles for 24
prompts: How many different rectangles can 24 make?
Which number in the twenties makes only one rectangle?

steps: Draw them on squared paper.
Try 23: what happens?

units.title: Counting in tens and fives
units.idea: Tens and fives make counting big numbers quick.
checks: Counts in 10s to 100
Counts in 5s to 50
prompts: How many tens in 50?
Count your fingers in fives.

steps: Count bundles of 10 to 100.
Colour multiples of 5 on the 100 square.
Count family fingers in 5s.

units.title: Threes, fours and fives
units.idea: Skip counting builds the 3, 4 and 5 times tables.
checks: Skip-counts the 3, 4 and 5 times tables
Recognises a cube number built from blocks
prompts: What is 4 lots of 3?
How many blocks in a 2 by 2 by 2 cube?

steps: Colour the 3s, 4s and 5s on a 100 square — spot the patterns.
Build a 2×2×2 cube and count.
Clap-and-count the tables.

units.title: Up to 100 and beyond
units.idea: 100 is ten tens; numbers keep going.
checks: Counts to 100
Says 100 is ten tens
prompts: How many tens make 100?
What comes after 99?

steps: Build 100 from ten bundles.
Count from 87 to 100 and back.
Find patterns down the columns of a 100 square.

units.title: Big patterns
units.idea: Patterns in numbers help us predict.
checks: Describes a number pattern and predicts the next term
prompts: What comes next: 1, 3, 6, 10…?
What is the rule?

steps: Build step squads and square numbers side by side.
Write the sequences and find the rule.
She invents a pattern for you.

units.title: Tables 6 to 9; turning arrays
units.idea: 3 × 4 is the same as 4 × 3 — turn the array.
checks: Shows 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 by turning an array
Skip-counts in 6s to 9s
prompts: Turn the rectangle: is it the same number?
What is 9 × 2? Trick: 10 × 2 take away 2.

steps: Draw a 3×4 array, cut it out, turn it.
Build the 6, 7, 8 and 9 tables on the 100 square.
Try the nines trick together.

units.title: Tens and ones (revisited)
units.idea: A two-digit number can be split into tens and ones in more than one way.
checks: Partitions a two-digit number into tens and ones in two ways
prompts: Is 34 three tens and four ones — or two tens and fourteen ones?

steps: Make 34 two different ways.
Add 23 + 14 with bundles.
Write the number sentence.

units.title: Hundreds and thousands
units.idea: Ten hundreds make a thousand; three-digit numbers.
checks: Reads and writes numbers to 999
Adds and subtracts within 99 using tens and ones
prompts: How many hundreds in 300?
What is 10 more than 245?

activity.materials: Bundles of 10 and 100 sticks (or paper strips)
steps: Build 245 from hundreds, tens and ones.
Read prices in a shop flyer.
Add two shopping amounts within 99.

units.title: Fractions
units.idea: A half is one of two equal parts; a quarter is one of four.
checks: Finds a half and a quarter of a shape
Finds a half of a small set (e.g. 8 grapes)
prompts: Are the two parts equal?
What is half of 8?

steps: Fold paper into halves and quarters.
Cut a roti fairly.
Share 8 grapes between two.
